questions.question: What does the function T(n) represent in running-time analysis?
gold_points: T(n) represents the running time for an input of size n.
It can be interpreted as number of time units or operation count.
It summarizes performance as a function of input size.
gold_source: Section 3.3 Measuring Running Time, PDF pages 4-5 (book pages 92-93)

questions.question: Why does the chapter use big-oh notation instead of exact time formulas?
gold_points: Big-oh hides constant factors that depend on machine and compiler details.
It focuses on growth behavior rather than exact implementation constants.
It enables clearer comparison of algorithm scalability.
gold_source: Section 3.4 Big-Oh and Approximate Running Time, PDF pages 8-9 (book pages 96-97)

questions.question: Explain step-by-step how the chapter estimates the running time of a simple for-loop using a numbered list.
gold_points: Bound the time required for one iteration of the loop body.
Multiply that per-iteration bound by the number of iterations.
Treat initialization and final test as lower-order O(1) terms that are usually neglected.
gold_source: Section 3.6 Analyzing the Running Time of a Program, PDF pages 23-24 (book pages 111-112)
